    tsdst.distributions.weibull_regression_post¶

    tsdst.distributions.weibull_regression_post(parms, X, Y, status=None, l_scale=1, neg=False, log=True, *, regression_parameter='shape', shared_prior=None)[source]¶

    Evaluate a Weibull regression posterior with a selectable regression parameter.

    Parameters:
    parmsnumpy.ndarray

    Intercept and regression coefficients, followed by the log of the shared distribution parameter. The coefficients model log shape when regression_parameter=’shape’, or log scale when it is ‘scale’.

    Xnumpy.ndarray

    Design matrix with a leading column of ones for the intercept.

    Ynumpy.ndarray

    Positive event or right-censoring times, one per design row.

    statusarray-like of zero or one, optional

    One denotes an observed event; zero denotes right censoring. None treats all times as observed events.

    l_scalefloat, optional

    Positive Laplace slope-prior scale. The default is 1. Each slope contributes abs(beta)/l_scale to the negative log posterior.

    negbool, optional

    Negate the selected density or log density. The default is False.

    logbool, optional

    Return log density when True. The default is True.

    regression_parameter{‘shape’, ‘scale’}, optional

    Distribution parameter modeled as exp(X @ coefficients). The other parameter is a shared positive scalar. The default is ‘shape’.

    shared_priorpair of float, optional

    Gamma(shape, scale) hyperparameters for the shared positive parameter. None uses (0.01, 100) for shared Weibull scale in shape regression, or (2, 1) for shared Weibull shape in scale regression.

    Returns:
    float

    Posterior density or log density, optionally negated. The density is defined on the sampled coefficient and log-shared-parameter scale.

    Notes

    The intercept prior is normal with mean zero and standard deviation 10. Slope priors are Laplace with scale l_scale. The final log parameter has a Gamma prior on its exponentiated value, so parms[-1] supplies the log-scale Jacobian. The coefficients have priors on their sampled scale; their log link does not require another Jacobian.

    Scale regression with a shared shape is a Weibull accelerated failure time and proportional hazards model. Shape regression with a shared scale generally has neither interpretation. The shared parameter is sampled, rather than held at a known value. See BayesWeibullRegressor for coefficient interpretations.

    Events contribute log density and right-censored times contribute log survival. Both branches use the matching observation’s shape and scale.
